GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-03-27T19:13:44Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Best way to include many-to-many self-referenced
Description: My User model has this...

```
User.hasMany(User, {
    as: 'Friends',
    foreignKey: 'FriendId',
    through: 'friends'
})
```

Sequelize has created this table...

```
CREATE TABLE friends
(
  "createdAt" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
  "updatedAt" timestamp with time zone NOT NULL,
  "FriendId" integer NOT NULL,
  "FriendsId" integer NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT friends_pkey PRIMARY KEY ("FriendId", "FriendsId")
)
WITH (
  OIDS=FALSE
);
```

My intention is to populate this table with 2 rows for every "friendship"; Friend A to Friend B and Friend B to Friend A.  So far so, good.

However, I'm stumped as to how I would join to this table with an include in Sequelize.  I also don't want the whole friends' User object if the current User is friends with the User being pulled in the main find.  I only really need to know if they are friends.  The following is the best I can come up with but it throws an error:

```
include: [
    {
        model: User,
        as: "Friends",
        required: false,
        where: {
            FriendsId: req.user.id
        }
    }
]
```

```
}
```
